items.title: From conditional detailed balance to a retained-coordinate joint kernel

source.attribution: ASTIS standard source-neutral mathematical derivation from pinned Mathlib definitions (Apache 2.0), not a quoted or numbered theorem of PBPS. Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang supply the motivating actual A.2/A.9 consumer; component-wise Gibbs is a second planned consumer.
source.anchor: Kernel.IsReversible, deterministic product and Measure.compProd: a.e. fiber-to-joint detailed balance

items.statement: Let \(A,B\) be arbitrary measurable spaces, \(\mu\) an s-finite measure on \(A\), \(R:A\rightsquigarrow B\) an s-finite kernel, and \(F:A\times B\rightsquigarrow B\) a jointly measurable s-finite kernel. Suppose that, for \(\mu\)-almost every \(a\), the kernel \(F_a(b,\cdot)=F((a,b),\cdot)\) is reversible under \(R(a,\cdot)\), in the sense of equality of nonnegative fluxes between every pair of measurable subsets of \(B\). Put \(\nu(da,db)=\mu(da)R(a,db)\). Then the transition \(L((a,b),d(a\prime,b\prime))=\delta_a(da\prime)F((a,b),db\prime)\), which retains the first coordinate, is reversible under \(\nu\). Neither the measures nor the kernels need be normalized or finite; zero measures, empty spaces and infinite fluxes are allowed.
assumptions: A kernel includes genuine measurability for every measurable output set. Joint measurability of F is a real premise encoded by its type; separate fiber measurability would not suffice for the disintegration argument.

The s-finite assumptions select the meaningful pinned Mathlib compProd and kernel-product interfaces. They are not asserted to be logically minimal for every possible independently defined extension. Outside these classes, totalized zero defaults must not be used as mathematical evidence.

The fiber detailed-balance premise holds simultaneously for all measurable fiber sets outside one mu-null set. Its good set needs no separately supplied measurability certificate. Joint-set sections are measurable preimages, not projections.

No Markov, probability, finite-mass, sigma-finite, Standard-Borel, topology, measurable-singleton, nonempty or real-integrability premise is present. All flux integrals are nonnegative and may be infinite.

This shared theorem does not construct a paper-specific conditional law. An actual PBPS or Gibbs adapter must identify its SAME selected R and joint disintegration. Detailed balance alone, without Markovness, is not an invariance assertion.
